summary: Two numbers that decide when a metric stops being fine — and the bands they create.

pairs.dont: Add a `direction` prop, or flip the bands by hand.
pairs.do: Put the thresholds in the order the metric means and let the bands follow.
pairs.why: `critical < warning` is what "low is bad" means. A separate flag is a second source of truth that can disagree with the numbers, and the disagreement is invisible until someone is paged.

pairs.dont: Rely on the red, amber and green bands to say which is which.
pairs.do: Keep the Critical and Warning labels above the thumbs.
pairs.why: The bands are three hues along one bar, which is the hardest case for anyone with a red-green deficiency. The label over each thumb is what survives; the colour reinforces it.

pairs.dont: Let one threshold pass the other, or clamp silently to the track ends.
pairs.do: Bound each thumb by its twin, and say so with aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax.
pairs.why: Crossed thresholds invert the bands and mean nothing. A screen reader that is told the range is 0–100 when the real bound is 85 gives an answer the control will not honour.

pairs.dont: Show bare numbers and put the unit in the field label.
pairs.do: Pass `format` so −80 reads as −80 dBm and 70 as 70%.
pairs.why: Thresholds get read out of context — in a summary, an alert, a screen reader. A number with no unit is a number someone has to go and look up.

pairs.dont: Use it to report where a metric currently sits.
pairs.do: Keep it for setting the two boundaries; show the live reading elsewhere.
pairs.why: It is a configuration control. Putting the current value on the same bar makes the thing you are editing and the thing you are watching look like one control.

a11y: Two thumbs, each role="slider" with its own aria-label, aria-valuenow and an aria-valuetext that is the formatted value — "-80 dBm", not "-80".
Each thumb's aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax are bounded by its twin as well as by the track, so the announced range always matches what the thumb can actually do.
Disabled sets aria-disabled and tabIndex -1 but leaves the thumbs in the accessibility tree. A disabled control is still something you may need to read.
Arrow keys move by step, Page by ten steps, Home and End to the bounds.
